post.description: Where to read or publish the exposure at its gateway by one of its protocols, with the short-lived credential that admits the caller there: a MoQ relay, path and token, or a URL (such as a WebRTC WHEP or WHIP endpoint) and a token to present as a bearer token, or as the URL's `jwt` query parameter where the protocol has no headers (RTSP, RTMP). `renditions` lists what the connection carries: the rendition chosen, or with `moq` every rendition the exposure offers, as tracks. Ask again before `expiresAt`, when the gateway stops admitting the caller. Members read, signed in. Devices call with an RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature by their own identity, as for `reports.submit`: they publish the exposures they are the pinned publisher of, and read those exposures' upstreams.

post.description: Events (such as a heartbeat, or whether video is being received), metric samples and log messages, about any subjects, in one batch of at most 1000 and 1 MiB. Any device: the request carries an RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature by the device's Ed25519 identity, with its public ID as `keyid`, covering the method, URL, `Content-Type` and RFC 9530 `Content-Digest`, with `created`, `expires` and a single-use `nonce`. The batch is stored or refused whole. Reports are not deduplicated: a retry is signed again, and may be stored twice.

post.description: The relay the signing device's iroh endpoint uses, with any token it needs, and the lease admitting the endpoint to it when the relay requires one. Every device gets the same relay, so a device is reached at its endpoint ID on that relay, with no address lookup. Asked for each time the device binds an endpoint, and again before its lease expires: the relay refuses new connections after that. Any device: the request carries an RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature by the device's Ed25519 identity, as for `reports.submit`, over an empty body.

401.description: The signature is missing, wrong, stale or replayed, its device is unknown, or the body does not match its digest

403.description: The relay will never admit the device's endpoint: it is denied, or leased to another service

412.description: The selected operation version is not served

503.description: The database is unavailable, or the relay cannot lease the endpoint

get.description: What the signing device runs, derived from the topology whenever it asks. `state` is `idle` for a device that runs nothing: an agent that is not its network's active agent, or whose network has no MediaMTX gateway. It is `active` for a network's active agent, with the MediaMTX gateway on its network (and how it checks readers' tokens), the MediaMTX `paths` it serves, each delivering one rendition of an exposure from a `source` that is a URL to pull while it is read (a camera's, credentials included) or another of its paths, and the `publishers` it runs, each publishing an exposure by MoQ in the `layout` its gateway takes, reading each rendition from one of its paths, with the `connect` ask for where to publish and the token to do so. `diagnostics` says what the topology asks for that the configuration leaves out, and why. Any device: the request carries an RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature by the device's Ed25519 identity, as for `reports.submit`, over an empty body.

401.description: The signature is missing, wrong, stale or replayed, its device is unknown, or the body does not match its digest

412.description: The selected operation version is not served

put.description: The addresses the signing device can be reached at on its own network, as it finds them on its interfaces: at most 32, each once, at most one `preferred` (the one its default route leaves by). They replace whatever it reported before, whole: an empty list leaves it with none. Members read them with `organisations.devices.listAddresses`. Any device: the request carries an RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature by the device's Ed25519 identity, as for `reports.submit`.

401.description: The signature is missing, wrong, stale or replayed, its device is unknown, or the body does not match its digest

412.description: The selected operation version is not served

address.description: An IPv4 or IPv6 address of the device, without a scope.

interface.description: The interface it was found on, as the device names it, such as `eth0` or `en0`.

preferred.description: Whether this is the address the device's default route leaves by: at most one is.

addresses.description: The addresses, in no order. Empty when the device found none it can be reached at.

get.description: The signing device's ID, organisation and kind: a device holds only its key, so it asks for the ID it reports about itself as. Any device: the request carries an RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature by the device's Ed25519 identity, as for `reports.submit`, over an empty body.

get.summary: Read a metric series over a time range

post.description: Events (such as a heartbeat, or whether video is being received), metric samples and log messages, about any subjects, in one batch of at most 1000 and 1 MiB. Any device: the request carries an RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature by the device's Ed25519 identity, with its public ID as `keyid`, covering the method, URL, `Content-Type` and RFC 9530 `Content-Digest`, with `created`, `expires` and a single-use `nonce`. The batch is stored or refused whole. Reports are not deduplicated: a retry is signed again, and may be stored twice.

post.description: The relay the signing device's iroh endpoint uses, with any token it needs, and the lease admitting the endpoint to it when the relay requires one. Every device gets the same relay, so a device is reached at its endpoint ID on that relay, with no address lookup. Asked for each time the device binds an endpoint, and again before its lease expires: the relay refuses new connections after that. Any device: the request carries an RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature by the device's Ed25519 identity, as for `reports.submit`, over an empty body.

401.description: The signature is missing, wrong, stale or replayed, its device is unknown, or the body does not match its digest

403.description: The relay will never admit the device's endpoint: it is denied, or leased to another service

412.description: The selected operation version is not served

503.description: The database is unavailable, or the relay cannot lease the endpoint

get.description: What the signing device runs, derived from the topology whenever it asks. `state` is `idle` for a device that runs nothing: an agent that is not its network's active agent, or whose network has no MediaMTX gateway. It is `active` for a network's active agent, with the MediaMTX gateway on its network (and how it checks readers' tokens), the MediaMTX `paths` it serves, each delivering one rendition of an exposure from a `source` that is a URL to pull while it is read (a camera's, credentials included) or another of its paths, and the `publishers` it runs, each publishing an exposure by MoQ in the `layout` its gateway takes, reading each rendition from one of its paths, with the `connect` ask for where to publish and the token to do so. `diagnostics` says what the topology asks for that the configuration leaves out, and why. Any device: the request carries an RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature by the device's Ed25519 identity, as for `reports.submit`, over an empty body.

401.description: The signature is missing, wrong, stale or replayed, its device is unknown, or the body does not match its digest

put.description: The addresses the signing device can be reached at on its own network, as it finds them on its interfaces: at most 32, each once, at most one `preferred` (the one its default route leaves by). They replace whatever it reported before, whole: an empty list leaves it with none. Members read them with `organisations.devices.listAddresses`. Any device: the request carries an RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature by the device's Ed25519 identity, as for `reports.submit`.

401.description: The signature is missing, wrong, stale or replayed, its device is unknown, or the body does not match its digest

412.description: The selected operation version is not served

address.description: An IPv4 or IPv6 address of the device, without a scope.

interface.description: The interface it was found on, as the device names it, such as `eth0` or `en0`.

preferred.description: Whether this is the address the device's default route leaves by: at most one is.

addresses.description: The addresses, in no order. Empty when the device found none it can be reached at.
